headline: Trump takes credit for Netanyahu showing, says he will 'take a look' at helping a Netanyahu-led unity government

sources: Donald Trump interview with Axios; US official to The Times of Israel; Reuters analysis via Deccan Herald/Japan Times
fault_line: Should Washington broker Israel's next government to keep its Iran-war partner in place -- or is that voters' verdict being overridden, with Arab parties as kingmakers?

sections.what_happened: [PRIMARY-SOURCE CLAIM + ATTRIBUTED REPORT] Trump told Axios Netanyahu is in 'pretty good shape' after early 'horror reports' about his prospects, claimed 'I heard my endorsement made a big difference for Bibi,' and, asked whether he would help form a Netanyahu-led unity government, said 'I will take a look.' A US official told The Times of Israel the White House had NOT decided whether to intervene in coalition talks, calling reports of a US preference for specific coalition arrangements inaccurate and premature while counting continues. Standing seat picture unchanged: Netanyahu bloc 53, Eisenkot bloc 48, Arab-led parties 19, neither reaching the 61-seat majority. Daily Sabah (T3, opinion/analysis) separately reports, citing Israeli media, that figures close to Trump held private discussions about a Netanyahu-Eisenkot unity government with Netanyahu as PM for up to two years before handing over -- ATTRIBUTION ONLY, not counted as corroboration of any plan, and not verified by the Axios/Reuters material retrieved.
sections.what_verified: 3 declared families: Axios T2 (interview quotes) + Reuters T1 (deadlock analysis, via Deccan Herald/Japan Times) + Times of Israel T3 (US official 'undecided'). The QUOTES are strongly supported; any US unity-government PLAN is not -- the White House position retrieved is explicitly undecided, and the Daily Sabah two-year-rotation detail is single-outlet analysis.
sections.what_disputed: YaLibnan's rendering of the same Axios exchange has Trump saying he 'hadn't thought about it' on unity involvement -- variant wording across carriers, same non-committal substance; do not present 'will take a look' as a commitment. Trump's claim that his endorsement changed the outcome is his own claim, with no verified evidence of effect on voting behaviour retrieved. Eisenkot has previously rejected serving under Netanyahu including in rotation (per Indian Express analysis, carrier undeclared -- attribution only). Netanyahu remains caretaker PM during bargaining.
sections.why_matters: Trump is now openly shopping himself into Israel's coalition talks -- 'I will take a look' at a unity government -- while his own White House says no decision has been made. Deadlock: 53-48-19, and 61 is the number that matters.
sections.context: Background: MISSED CATCH-UP (Axios interview Wed Oct 28, in no prior Oct 29 scan as a standalone item) -- Trump takes credit for Netanyahu showing, says he will 'take a look' at helping a Netanyahu-led unity government; White House undecided

totw_analysis: Our read: Trump is now openly shopping himself into Israel's coalition talks -- 'I will take a look' at a unity government -- while his own White House says no decision has been made. Deadlock: 53-48-19, and 61 is the number that matters. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Should Washington broker Israel's next government to keep its Iran-war partner in place -- or is that voters' verdict being overridden, with Arab parties as kingmakers?
